summary: Forest Lookouts index lists a Brownfield tower in Laclede County, Mark Twain NF; no history, height or status found in any source read.

evidence.supports: tower listed in Laclede County, Mark Twain National Forest, 34N-13W-20
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Laclede County - Mark Twain National Forest - 34N-13W-20

evidence.supports: Brownfield is an unincorporated community in northeastern Laclede County
evidence.quote: Brownfield is an unincorporated community in northeastern Laclede County

evidence.supports: community just over a mile southeast of the Laclede-Pulaski county line and a mile east of Route K
evidence.quote: The community is located just over one mile southeast of the Laclede- Pulaski county line and one mile east of Missouri Route K

evidence.supports: community within Mark Twain NF; Gasconade River one mile east
evidence.quote: It is within the Mark Twain National Forest and the Gasconade River lies just one mile to the east.
A post office called Brownfield was established in 1930, and remained in operation until 1955.

evidence.supports: named for Riley Brownfield, an early postmaster
evidence.quote: Riley Brownfield, an early postmaster, gave the community his last name.

evidence.supports: 1954 map: Brownfield School and two houses of worship nearby
evidence.quote: In the mid-1950s, the small settlement of Brownfield served as a local hub, supported by the Brownfield School and two houses of worship

evidence.supports: map is a USGS topographic map
Brownfield Missionary Church on the map's feature list

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The Forest Lookouts Brownfield page holds only its heading and the grid location; no build date, builder, height, staffing, fate or status was found. Two WebSearch calls and one websearch.py query returned no tower history. Living New Deal and Missouri Life pages returned HTTP 403. The Pastmaps 1954 description names a separate Fairview Lookout Tower on high ground near the Fairview community; no source read ties that tower to the Brownfield record, so the two should not be merged. Record coordinates 37.6415, -92.3794 were not checked against any map. Record height_m is null and status unknown, and that remains so. A Forest Service records inquiry (Mark Twain National Forest) is the next step.
